summary: Kyojun Shimizutani was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University. He held positions at Taisho University and served as kanju at Senso-ji circa 1974 to 1979.

Kyoko Fujii is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1970 to 1978. She held professorships at Yokohama City, Hamamatsu, Hokkaido, and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.
Kyoko Tokuno specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She held an academic post at the University of Oregon and served as a professor at the University of Washington, attested in 2017.
Kyoshi Renja is a Buddhist studies scholar who pursued doctoral studies at Taisho University, attested in 2013, and held a research student post there.

Kyosho Hayashima was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who taught Shinjo Kawasaki. His career included posts at Toyo University and Yokohama City University in 1962, and as a professor at the University of Tokyo in 1980.
Kyosho Tanaka is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1970 to 1977. He served as an associate professor at Musashino University from circa 1975 to 2018.
Kyoshun Todo was a Buddhist studies scholar who held faculty positions at Bukkyo University, serving as an assistant professor in 1962 and as a professor from around 1988 to 1992.
Kōdō Yotsuya is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed an MA at Komazawa University and earned a PhD from the University of Hamburg.
Kōichi Furusaka is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Hakuyu Hadano. He served as a professor at Osaka Kyoiku University, attested in 1991.
Laeticia Söderman is a Buddhist studies and Japanology scholar who completed an M.A. in 2010 and pursued graduate studies at the University of Helsinki, attested in 2014.

Lal Mani Joshi was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Allahabad, Banaras Hindu University, and Gorakhpur University under Govind Chandra Pande, later teaching at Haverford College.
Lalchandra Bhagawandas Gandhi worked in Indology, serving as a Jain Pandit at Baroda Central Library and holding a post at the Oriental Institute, Vadodara, attested in 1939.

Lama Palden Drolma is a practitioner and scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied under traditional teachers including Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, Dudjom Rinpoche, Situ Rinpoche, and Jamgön Kongtrül the Third, among others.
Lama Yeshe Gyamtso is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under the traditional teachers Lama Norlha and Kalu Rinpoche.

Lambert Schmithausen studied under Erich Frauwallner and Paul Hacker. A scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, he held professorships at the University of Münster (circa 1970–1976) and the University of Hamburg (1973–2005).

Lance E. Nelson specializes in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He completed his doctoral thesis at McMaster University in 1986 and held a professorship at the University of San Diego, attested in 1997.

Lance S. Cousins was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He held posts at the University of Manchester, Wolfson College, and the University of Oxford, and served as president of the Pali Text Society from circa 1994 to 2002.
Lang Chen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned a PhD at Yale University, attested in 2015. She studied under Janet Gyatso, Koichi Shinohara, and Phyllis Granoff.

Lang Eun Ra is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who completed doctoral studies at Temple University under Charles Wei-hsun Fu, also studying with Bibhuti S. Yadav, Norbert M. Samuelson, and Leonard Swidler.
Lara Braitstein is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. She earned her PhD from McGill University, where she studied under Richard P. Hayes.
